key_insight: GenEHR combines generative modeling of patient histories with supervised adaptation to identify cohorts at elevated risk of a first cancer diagnosis within five years.
clinical_relevance: The approach could help prioritize high-risk patients for screening and prevention, but its clinical utility requires prospective evaluation.
method: Train an autoregressive model on longitudinal EHRs from millions of patients.
Model diagnoses, medications, lab values, procedures, and irregular intervals between visits.
Use parameter-efficient supervised adaptation for risk stratification across 17 cancer types.
evidence_signal: Retrospective evaluation in five large EHR cohorts found that supervised adaptation substantially improved five-year cancer prediction performance; the abstract reports no numerical metrics.
watch_item: Prospective validation is needed to establish whether risk-guided screening improves outcomes without excessive false positives or unnecessary procedures.
paper_title: Identifying cohorts at elevated risk of cancers using generative modeling of patient health states
